references.text: The people baked unleavened bread from the dough they had brought with them from Egypt, for they were driven out and could not wait, and they had not prepared food for the journey.
For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. On the first day itself you shall remove leaven from your houses.
Moses reminds the people to remember this day when they came out of Egypt, and that they shall not eat leavened bread.
Unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days, and no leaven shall be found among the people.
The Israelites were to carry valuables on their shoulders when they left Egypt, just as here they are carrying the dough on their shoulders.
Reminder to eat unleavened bread for seven days as a memorial of the haste with which they left Egypt.
Paul uses leaven as a symbol of sin and urges the church to be unleavened, referring to Christ as the Passover lamb.
